parsed.notes: Lens B only; support and quote-fidelity merits were not independently reviewed.

reasons: The lake identity is verified and matches Townsend v. Sain, U.S. Supreme Court, decided 1963-03-18, with official citation 372 U.S. 293.
The lake treatment marks field_i_validity as good_law as of 2026-06-30, with the caveat directed to a separate habeas-procedure branch rather than the existence of the cited authority.
residual_risks: The case should not be presented as globally good for its federal habeas evidentiary-hearing standard.
reviewed.suggested_tightening: Tie current-law use of the citation to the confession-voluntariness holding.

reasons: Lens B does not retest support or quote fidelity.
For currency only, the lake scope note preserves good law on the confession-voluntariness holding for a drug/'truth serum'-induced confession not the product of a free intellect.
The disclosed negative progeny edges are proposed, point-null, and marked as mentioned; the final lake treatment does not mark the confession-voluntariness point overruled or superseded.
residual_risks: Support and exact holding language remain for Lens A.
Colorado v. Connelly appears as a proposed criticized edge with no point detail, leaving a treatment-audit risk.
reviewed.suggested_tightening: Keep the holding framed as the surviving confession-voluntariness rule, separate from habeas procedure.

reasons: Lens B does not retest the editorial support basis for the home-role label.
The home is Due-Process Voluntariness of Confessions, and the lake scope note preserves the confession-voluntariness holding as good law.
The disclosed treatment caveat targets a separate federal-habeas evidentiary-hearing standard, not the due-process confession home.
residual_risks: The role label could be overread if reused on a habeas-procedure page without the caveat.
reviewed.suggested_tightening: Carry the habeas-procedure caveat wherever the case is displayed outside the confession-voluntariness home.

defect.evidence_quote:
varies_by_point: false
  scope_note: "Good law on the confession-voluntariness holding (a drug/'truth serum'-induced confession not the product of a free intellect is inadmissible). The separate federal-habeas evidentiary-hearing standard (the Townsend circumstances/deliberate-bypass) was abrogated by Keeney v. Tamayo-Reyes, 504 U.S. 1 (1992), and superseded by AEDPA, 28 U.S.C. §2254(e)(2)."
defect.problem: The good-law treatment survives as scoped, but the metadata says varies_by_point=false even though the same disclosed treatment note identifies one surviving point and one abrogated/superseded point.
defect.proposed_fix: Set varies_by_point to true and add point overrides distinguishing the confession-voluntariness holding as good_law from the federal habeas evidentiary-hearing/deliberate-bypass branch as abrogated by Keeney and superseded by AEDPA.

reasons: The disclosed lake/page treatment supports good_law only on the confession-voluntariness holding.
The same disclosed treatment says the separate habeas-procedure standard was abrogated and superseded.
No disclosed record refutes the scoped confession-voluntariness good-law treatment itself; the defect is the point-variation metadata and flat status presentation.
residual_risks: The lake treatment derivation records audit_needed, cap_hit, and proposed negative events, so later audit could refine point overrides.
reviewed.suggested_tightening: Render status as good on confession voluntariness, with habeas hearing standard abrogated/superseded, instead of an unqualified good badge.

reasons: The lake identity lists court as U.S. Supreme Court and court_level as scotus.
The page authority_weight of Binding — SCOTUS matches the disclosed court identity.
The treatment caveat limits which holding remains binding, but does not change the institutional weight of a surviving Supreme Court holding.
residual_risks: Without the treatment caveat, the weight label could be overread to include the abrogated habeas-procedure standard.
reviewed.suggested_tightening: Pair the weight label with the point-specific treatment caveat on downstream cards.
